subject: Syntax highlighting with text where one of the quotation marks is off the screen

messages.author: 8e300cba64490d91
messages.subject: Syntax highlighting with text where one of the quotation marks is off the screen
parts:
Hi,

I wanted to ask about this minor issue I have. Whenever there is some text in the code, but one of the quotation marks is off the screen, then the syntax highlighting erroneously believes the text starts at the second quotation mark. E.g., say you have:

x <- "Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipisicing elit, sed do eiusmod
tempor incididunt ut labore et dolore magna aliqua. Ut enim ad minim veniam,
***quis nostrud exercitation ullamco laboris nisi ut aliquip ex ea commodo
consequat. Duis aute irure dolor in reprehenderit in voluptate velit esse cillum
dolore eu fugiat nulla pariatur. Excepteur sint occaecat cupidatat non proident,
sunt in culpa qui officia deserunt mollit anim id est laborum."


y <- runif(10)
nchar(x)
# Etc.

Say the top of the screen is at ***, then the second " will be interpreted (apparently) as the first quotation mark, and the subsequent lines shown in the colour corresponding to character text. Moving up and down the screen eventually fixes that.

Do you know if this is specific to vim-r-plugin, or more generally an issue of syntax highlighting in vim?

Many thanks!

parts: I should also add that this doesn't always happens, just sometimes, which is the odd thing.

messages.author: b256a2742aacd200
messages.subject: Re: Syntax highlighting with text where one of the quotation marks is off the screen
parts:
This happens because there is no "syntax sync" in syntax/r.vim. I just added "syntax sync minlines=40" to syntax/r.vim (at github). This might solve the specific problem reported, but may also make syntax highlight for R slow, specially if fold is enabled. Users can control the value of minlines by setting the value of r_syn_minlines in their vimrc. Example:

let r_syn_minlines = 400
